full_judgment:
Md. Ashfaqul Islam J: At the instance of the petitioner, Mostafa Ahmed this Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why Order dated 22-3-2011 passed by Artha Rin Adalat and Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet in Artha Jari Case No. 01 of 20 II arising out of Artha Rin Case No. 62 of 1990 rejecting the petitioner's application under section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissing the execution proceeding as time barred Annexure-C to the Writ Petition and order dated 30-3-2011 passed by Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet in Artha Jari Case No. 01 of 2011 issuing a warrant of arrest against the petitioner (Annexure-E) to the Writ Petition should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. At the time of issuing Rule operation of the order as envisaged in Annexure 'C' dated 22-3-2011 and order dated 30-3-2011 Annexure-'E' was stayed by this Division. 

 2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that, the petitioner on 31-10-1985 filed an application to the plaintiff-respondent Sonali bank Limited, Khadimnagar Branch, Sylhet for a loan in order to purchase Minibus and was favoured with the same by the bank. Loan was sanctioned back in the year 1986. Subsequently the petitioner failed to repay the loan money for which respondent bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 62 of 1990 which on contest resulted in passing of judgment and decree dated 27-10-1990 against which the respondent bank preferred First Appeal No. 451 of 1991 before the High Court Division which subsequently on 13-5-2010 was dismissed for non-prosecution as a result of withdrawal of the appeal by the appellant-bank. Thereafter, the bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 01 of 2011 on 24-1-2011 in which the present petitioner filed an application before the Artha Rin Adalat (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) under section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain) contending that the said Artha Jari Case cannot proceed being barred by limitation under section 28 of the Ain. By the impugned order dated 22-3-2011 the Adalat rejected the application and issued order of warrant or arrest against the petitioner. The petitioner challenging the order of rejection dated 22-3-2011 and- the order of issuing warrant of arrest has moved this Division and obtained the present Rule and stay. 

 3. Mr. AKM Rezaul Karim appearing with Mr. Saleh Mahmood Naheed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner after placing the petition, different Annexure and the order impugned against argued that the Artha Jari Case No. 01 of 2011 filed by the respondent-bank is clearly time barred as per provision of section 28(1) of the A in which states that Artha Execution Case should be filed within one year from the date of passing of the decree. In the present case the judgment and decree was passed on 27-10-1990 and the Execution Case was filed on 24-1-2011 i.e. after a long lapse of 20 years from the passing of the decree and, as such, the Artha Execution Case is barred by limitation and the concerned Adalat has no jurisdictiori to entertain the same and therefore it is liable to be dismissed as per section 28(2) of the Ain. Next he submits that consequently the order of warrant of arrest passed by the Adalat under section 34 of the Ain is also illegal inasmuch as, the same has been issued without complying with the obligation to be fulfilled under law before so doing. 

 4. Mr. ABM Bayezid, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2-Sonali Bank, on the other hand, by filing affidavit-in-opposition vehemently opposes the Rule and submits that the order impugned against is absolutely a proper order which has been passed in keeping with section 28 of the Ain. Substantiating his argument the learned Advocate submits that First Appeal No. 451 of 1991 was preferred by the bank against the part decree passed in Artha Rin Suit No. 62 of 1990 before this Division which was subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution at the instance of the bank and right after that the bank filed the Artha Execution Case under section 28(1) of the Ain and there is no wrong in it. He further submits that the disposal of the appeal in any manner is the date of disposal of the suit since the appeal is the continuation of the suit. Therefore, it is needless to mention that in the case in hand the appeal ended with the order of non-prosecution and duly Execution Case was filed within one year as required under section 28(1) of the Ain. There being no illegality in filing of the said Execution Case this Rule on that score should be discharged outright. 

 6. The moot question that faces this Division in this petition is whether under the facts and circumstances of the case both the order impugned against have been passed in gross violation of the mandatory implication of section 28(1) and section 34 of the Ain and would operate as a bar in filing of the Artha Execution Case No. 01 of 2011 and issuing order of Civil imprisonment. 

 10. If we glean the aforesaid provision together it appears that the law enjoins that an Execution Case should mandatorily be filed in absolute compliance of section 28(1) of Ain as stated above. The law on the point is very much clear that notwithstanding anything different contained in Limitation Act and in the Code of Civil Procedure the time prescribed for filing of the Execution Case under section 28 of Ain should be strictly followed. Moreover, the law, being a specially shall override any other provisions in that regard. Nobody refutes this settled proposition of law. But in the instant case admittedly the suit was decreed in part in the year 1990 against which the respondent Sonali Bank being aggrieved preferred First Appeal No. 451 of 1991 before this Division and it is also admitted that on 13-5-2010 the said appeal was dismissed for non- prosecution at the instance of the bank. It is also admitted that all these days the petitioner kept mum and did not even file any cross appeal to ventilate his grievances whatsoever. Admittedly the petitioner has no grievance against the part decree rather respondent bank was aggrieved against the said decree and proceeded against the same by filing First Appeal. 

 11. Now the petitioner has come before this Division mainly on the ground that the First Appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution and twenty years thereafter the respondent Sonali Bank filed Execution Case which is ex facie barred under section 28(1) of the Ain. This argument is fallacious and untenable. The question of limitation is a mixed question of fact and law. One cannot be allowed to take advantage of something indirectly which he cannot take directly. The petitioner all of a sudden has come up with a feeble argument that the Execution Case is barred by limitation since it has been filed after 20 years though he did not part with the appeal in any manner. What more is required to hold that only to bring the case within the mischief of section 28(1) he has dragged this case before this Division on a frivolous ground which is absolutely bereft of any consideration whatsoever? Therefore we find substance in the argument of the learned counsel for the respondent Bank that the disposal of the appeal in any manner is the date of disposal of the suit since the appeal is the continuation of the suit and for that reason no illegality as such in filing of the said Execution Case have been committed. 

 12. Since the point raised as regard the Execution Case has been decided let us now digress to next point of subsequent order of warrant of arrest in the execution case which is also under challenge in this rule. In terms of ratio decidendi of the Appellate Division in the case of Provat Kumar Das vs Manager Agrani Bank, Main Branch Shahab Bazar, Rajshahi 15 MLR (AD) 96 = 15 BLC (AD) 113 and in several cases by this Division regarding warrant of arrest or Civil imprisonment as contained in section 34 of the Ain 2003 it has been held that the said law is absolutely independent and self-contained. Our Appellate Division maintained that the above provision of section 34 is exclusive, independent and exhaustive which cannot be subjected to or circumvent by other provisions of Ain. The Appellate Division observed:- 

 "It appears that the section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is clear and provides for ordering civil imprisonment upto 6 months against a judgment-debtor for compelling to satisfy the decree. Section-34 is not dependant upon section 33. In the instant case, the decree holder has taken step for auction sale of the property but there being no response, auction sale could not be held. Further it appears from the provisions of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 that the law provides for simple civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor to compel to make the payment for satisfaction of the decree and is not an alternative punishment in lieu of payment of the decretal amount. Civil imprisonment will not exempt payment of the decretal amount." 

 15. The ratio of Pro vat Kumar's case by now has been applied in several subsequent decisions. In a recent decision of Manik K Bhattachayria vs Artha Rin Adalat, 16 BLC 195 High Court Division has elaborated principle of civil imprisonment under section 34 of the Ain after discussing several decisions including Provat Kumar's case.
